q: מה נכון לגבי שאלון PHQ-9 לצורך איבחון ומעקב של דיכאון אצל קשישים?
o: תוצאה של 10 ומעלה בשאלון מחשידה ל- MAJOR DEPRESSION
החיסרון בשאלון הוא שאינו כולל הערכת אובדנות
השאלון יעיל לאבחנה, אך אינו רגיש מספיק להערכת יעילות של טיפול
תוצאה של 0-4 בשאלון מצריכה הערכה נוספת
explanation:
The **PHQ-9** supports depression screening and monitoring in older adults (p. 1012).

**A. A score of 10 or more raises suspicion of major depression.** Correct, the book says that this score typically correlates with major depression and warrants evaluation and intervention; it is a suspicious threshold, not a standalone diagnosis (p. 1012).
**B. The questionnaire's drawback is that it does not assess suicidality.** Wrong, item 9 asks about death wishes or self-harm, so suicidality is addressed (pp. 1010, 1012).
**C. It is useful for diagnosis but insufficiently sensitive to treatment effects.** Wrong, the source explicitly says it can document symptom changes during treatment, supporting monitoring as well as initial screening (p. 1012).
**D. A score of 0–4 requires further evaluation.** Wrong, this range indicates no depression or clinically insignificant symptoms; the score itself is not the threshold requiring the additional evaluation proposed here (pp. 1009, 1012).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1009–1010, 1012.

q: בן 90, במעקבך מזה כ-5 שנים בשל ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה. בנוסף סובל מאי ספיקה כלייתית עם פינוי קריאטינין של 35 מ"ל/דקה. עקב כאבי גב כרוניים מטופל ב- ZALDIAR (TRAMADOL+PRACETAMOL). בביקורת האחרונה היה עצוב, הרבה לבכות והביע מחשבות של חוסר ערך וחוסר תקווה. מהו שיקול נכון לגבי הטיפול בדיכאון במטופל זה?
o: אי ספיקה כלייתית מהווה קונטראינדיקציה למתן MIRTAZAPINE (MIRO )
טיפול ב- SSRI's בקשישים כרוך בסיכון מוגבר להתאבדות
טיפול ב- Venlafaxine בשילוב עם Tramadol יכול לגרום ל- Serotonin Syndrome
התועלת של פסיכותרפיה בזקנים עם דיכאון אינה משמעותית
explanation:
**Combining serotonergic drugs** requires caution: tramadol inhibits serotonin reuptake, and combining it with an antidepressant can cause serotonin syndrome. This is the relevant medication concern, rather than excluding depression treatment solely because of age or renal function (Hazzard 8e, pp. 788, 1061, 1653).
"May cause serotonin syndrome in combination with SSRIs or other antidepressants" (p. 1653).

**A. Renal impairment is a contraindication to mirtazapine (Miro).** Wrong, renal impairment reduces mirtazapine clearance and may require a dose decrease; it is not an absolute contraindication (mirtazapine prescribing information, sections 4 and 8.6).
**B. SSRI treatment in older adults increases suicide risk.** Wrong, the pooled trial analyses in the label did not show increased suicidality in adults aged 65 or older. Clinical monitoring is still required with any antidepressant treatment (mirtazapine prescribing information, section 5.1).
**C. Venlafaxine combined with tramadol can cause serotonin syndrome.** Correct, both act on serotonin reuptake; the combination fits the source's warning about tramadol with serotonergic antidepressants (Hazzard 8e, pp. 929, 1061, 1653).
**D. Psychotherapy has no meaningful benefit in older adults with depression.** Wrong, cognitive behavioral and interpersonal therapies can produce sustained improvements in mood and coping. Age does not justify dismissing their benefit (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 788, 929, 1014, 1061, 1653; Coupler LLC, mirtazapine prescribing information, 2024, sections 4, 5.1, 8.6, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=26aac059-4819-7ad4-e063-6394a90a9766.

q: בת 79, ברקע סוכרת מאוזנת והיפותירואידיזם, הופנתה על ידי רופא המשפחה לצורך המלצה בנוגע לטיפול תרופתי בדיכאון. הדיכאון אובחן לפני כחצי שנה ומאז קיבלה SERTRALINE (LUSTRAL) במינון של 50 מ"ג ליום, ללא הטבה בדיכאון ב-. נשללו בעיות רפואיות אחרות, מעבדה תקינה. קיימת היענות טובה לטיפול ואין למטופלת תופעות לוואי. מה ההמלצה להמשך הטיפול?
o: מאחר והחולה לא הגיבה לטיפול ב-SERTRALINE (LUSTRAL), מומלץ לשנות לתרופה חלופית מאותה הקבוצה (SSRI), כגון ESCITALOPRAM (CIPRALEX)
נוכח סבילות טובה לטיפול, מומלץ להמשיך בו ולהוסיף טיפול בתרופה מקבוצה אחרת כגון SNRI
מומלץ להעלות מינון של SERTRALINE (LUSTRAL) בהדרגה ל-100 מ"ג ביום ולבחון מחדש תועלת הטיפול מספר שבועות לאחר הגעה למינון זה
מומלץ ללכת במקביל לטיפול פסיכולוגי שכן הסבירות להשגת שיפור עם טיפול תרופתי בלבד הינה נמוכה
explanation:
**Official answer:** Gradually increase SERTRALINE (LUSTRAL) to 100 mg daily and reassess benefit several weeks after reaching that dose (IMA final answer key, 2020, question 65).
The source recommends **starting low and titrating gradually**, adapting dose to response and tolerability; the dose table lists a sertraline maximum of 200 mg daily (p. 1015, Figure 65-4; p. 929, Table 60-9). The stem reports good adherence, no adverse effects and no benefit at 50 mg. Increasing to 100 mg applies the titration principle within that range; it is not a mandatory dose for every patient. Measurable benefit generally takes six to eight weeks, supporting reassessment after several weeks at the new dose (p. 1014).

**A. Switch sertraline to another SSRI, such as escitalopram, because it has not worked.** Wrong, switching can be considered later, but an adequate trial with dose escalation should precede declaring failure of a tolerated drug. This is an inference from titration, not a prohibition on switching (p. 1015).
**B. Continue the tolerated drug and add another class, such as an SNRI.** Wrong, this adds treatment before completing titration of the tolerated drug. This is an inference from the flowchart, not a claim that combinations have no later role (p. 1015).
**C. Gradually increase sertraline to 100 mg daily and reassess several weeks later.** Correct, officially accepted; gradual escalation fits good tolerability and absent response at the current dose (p. 1015).
**D. Add psychotherapy because improvement with medication alone is unlikely.** Wrong, psychotherapy can help, but these data do not justify abandoning an adequate-dose medication trial or declaring medication benefit unlikely (pp. 1014-1015).
Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 929, 1014-1015.

q: מה הקשר בין דיכאון לבין מחלות "גופניות"?
o: דיכאון בחולי סרטן שכיח יותר בגברים
דיכאון יכול להיות תופעת לוואי שכיחה של טיפול ב- ACE INHIBITORS
דיכאון משני לשבר בצוואר הירך נוטה להמשיך לטווח ארוך
דיכאון בחולי סרטן נמצא בקורלציה עם חומרת הכאב
explanation:
**Pain and depression in cancer** are closely related, so assessment of physical symptoms should include mood. This relationship alone does not prove that treating pain prevents depression, and the source advises excluding other medical causes before diagnosing depression (p. 1392).
"Among patients with cancer, there is a strong relationship between pain and depression." (p. 1392).

**A. Depression in cancer patients is more common in men.** Wrong, the book identifies particular risk groups, including unmarried men and women with severe illness; it does not claim greater prevalence among all men as a group (p. 1392).
**B. Depression can be a common adverse effect of ACE inhibitors.** Wrong, absence of central nervous system adverse effects is described as an advantage of ACE inhibitors. Calling depression a common effect conflicts with that description, without implying an individual event is impossible (pp. 1225-1226).
**C. Depression following hip fracture tends to persist long term.** Wrong, according to the official key, but this is not a promise of rapid recovery. Depressive symptoms are described during admission and up to six months after fracture, with poorer recovery; the book does not establish a uniform tendency to persist beyond this (p. 799).
**D. Depression in cancer patients correlates with pain severity.** Correct, the relationship between pain and depression is explicit, supporting the option without establishing one-way causation (p. 1392).

Note: Long term has no defined duration in this question. The key is preserved, but this option must not be used to exclude persistent depression after a fracture.
Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 799, 1225-1226, 1392.

q: A 75-year-old man in rehabilitation after a stroke reports sadness, poor appetite, and low motivation. No assessment has yet distinguished subsyndromal symptoms from major depression. What is needed before selecting an antidepressant?
o: Select a small dose as drug treatment for subsyndromal depressive symptoms
Assess for major depression and establish his treatment preference
Select a uniform target dose for patients of his age
Begin at a full therapeutic dose to improve medication adherence
explanation:
**Assessment before prescribing** establishes whether the condition is amenable to antidepressant treatment and whether the patient wants it (p. 1015). For minor or subsyndromal depression, antidepressants "do not show evidence of benefit" (p. 1015). The chapter also favors individualized dosing and slow titration.

**A. Select a small dose as drug treatment for subsyndromal depressive symptoms.** Wrong, the source does not support treating minor or subsyndromal depression with a small antidepressant dose simply because symptoms are mild (p. 1015).
**B. Assess for major depression and establish his treatment preference.** Correct, the flowchart asks whether it is major depression and whether the patient wants an antidepressant before proceeding (p. 1015).
**C. Select a uniform target dose for patients of his age.** Wrong, the source describes the appropriate dose as the one that works for the individual, not a fixed age-based target (p. 1015).
**D. Begin at a full therapeutic dose to improve medication adherence.** Wrong, lower starting doses with gradual titration were associated with better adherence than higher initial doses in the cited discussion (p. 1015).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1015.

q: An older woman living in the community has depression with cognitive impairment, making management complex. Which specialist referral does Hazzard describe for this situation?
o: Geriatric mental health consultation for the combined presentation
General surgical consultation for assessment of cognitive function
Diagnostic radiology consultation for planning depression treatment
Physical medicine consultation for managing psychiatric medication
explanation:
**Specialist referral** is an option when depression and cognitive impairment make care complex. The source recommends the relevant specialty while emphasizing that referral does not guarantee benefit: "referral to a geriatric mental health specialist may provide the most benefit for the patient." (p. 1014).

**A. Geriatric mental health consultation for the combined presentation.** Correct, the source specifically identifies geriatric mental health expertise for complex depression with cognitive impairment (p. 1014).
**B. General surgical consultation for assessment of cognitive function.** Wrong, general surgery is not the specialty identified for this combined psychiatric and cognitive presentation (p. 1014).
**C. Diagnostic radiology consultation for planning depression treatment.** Wrong, diagnostic radiology does not match the geriatric mental health referral described for this treatment problem (p. 1014).
**D. Physical medicine consultation for managing psychiatric medication.** Wrong, physical medicine does not match the specialist service identified for complex depression with cognitive impairment (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1014.

q: A 79-year-old woman is diagnosed with major depression after evaluation of weight loss and withdrawal from social activities. She wishes to consider psychotherapy before starting medication. Which statement matches Hazzard?
o: Psychotherapy may be delivered as open-ended work without defined goals
Structured psychotherapy may improve mood and develop coping skills
Psychotherapy may be selected with no need to define treatment processes
The same psychotherapy may be continued without reviewing a lack of improvement
explanation:
**Structured psychotherapy** can improve mood and develop coping skills and insights. The studied approaches are short-term and goal-directed, and lack of improvement should prompt consideration that the modality is ineffective (p. 1014).
"Various types of psychotherapy, such as cognitive behavioral therapy and interpersonal therapy, can produce lasting improvements in mood, and development of coping skills and insights." (p. 1014).

**A. Psychotherapy may be delivered as open-ended work without defined goals.** Wrong, the studied approaches use clear goals and processes, rather than open-ended work without goals (p. 1014).
**B. Structured psychotherapy may improve mood and develop coping skills.** Correct, this reflects the benefits described for approaches such as cognitive behavioral and interpersonal therapy (p. 1014).
**C. Psychotherapy may be selected with no need to define treatment processes.** Wrong, clear treatment processes are part of the studied structured approaches (p. 1014).
**D. The same psychotherapy may be continued without reviewing a lack of improvement.** Wrong, the source advises reassessing effectiveness when improvement has not occurred, rather than continuing without review (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014.

q: An older man with depression, social withdrawal, and weight loss says there is no point in going on. Before adjusting medication, which assessment does Hazzard recommend for every depressed older patient?
o: Assessment of auditory memory and new learning
Assessment of suicidal thoughts, intent, and plans
Assessment of walking speed and handgrip strength
Assessment of exercise tolerance and respiratory function
explanation:
**Suicide risk assessment** is required in depressed older patients. It includes thoughts, intent, plans, and access to lethal means (p. 1008). "All depressed older patients should be assessed for suicide risk." (p. 1008).

**A. Assessment of auditory memory and new learning.** Wrong, memory testing does not assess the suicidal thoughts, intent, plans, and access to means specified by the recommendation (p. 1008).
**B. Assessment of suicidal thoughts, intent, and plans.** Correct, this addresses the stated risk domain; assessment should also include access to lethal means (p. 1008).
**C. Assessment of walking speed and handgrip strength.** Wrong, physical performance assessment does not substitute for the recommended suicide-risk inquiry (p. 1008).
**D. Assessment of exercise tolerance and respiratory function.** Wrong, cardiorespiratory assessment does not address the suicide-risk questions required by the cited recommendation (p. 1008).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1008.

q: An 81-year-old assisted-living resident is hospitalized with failure to thrive. He has lost 15 lb in three months, has a BMI of 19, and is withdrawn and eating poorly. He has mild dementia, depression, and BPH and takes sertraline 50 mg and tamsulosin 0.4 mg. Albumin is 2.8 g/dL and prealbumin 12 mg/dL. His son lives abroad and his daughter visits monthly. A social worker suggests hospice assessment. Which response addresses a potentially treatable contributor to his decline?
o: Treat the weight loss as establishing an irreversible terminal prognosis
Request specialist assessment of depression with cognitive impairment
Treat nutritional supplementation as replacing assessment of depression
Treat the antidepressant prescription as excluding depression-related poor intake
explanation:
**Depression can contribute to poor intake and weight loss** and may be treatable. With concurrent cognitive impairment, specialist mental-health assessment is supported for this complex presentation (pp. 410, 1014). "Depression is a highly prevalent, frequently unrecognized, and potentially treatable cause of a poor appetite and weight loss." (p. 410).

**A. Treat the weight loss as establishing an irreversible terminal prognosis.** Wrong, weight loss does not establish irreversibility when potentially treatable contributors remain; the hospice discussion requires assessment of prognosis and irreversibility (pp. 410, 1049).
**B. Request specialist assessment of depression with cognitive impairment.** Correct, depression with cognitive impairment is identified as a complex situation in which geriatric mental-health referral may benefit the patient (p. 1014).
**C. Treat nutritional supplementation as replacing assessment of depression.** Wrong, nutritional support does not assess the potentially treatable depressive cause of poor intake described by the source (p. 410; application to this case).
**D. Treat the antidepressant prescription as excluding depression-related poor intake.** Wrong, the prescription does not establish that depression has resolved. Reassessment is appropriate in a complex case with ongoing symptoms (p. 1014; inference from the case).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 410, 1014, 1049.

q: An 83-year-old woman with depression has a partial response and adverse effects during antidepressant treatment. After clinical reassessment, she and her clinician agree on a medication change. Which principle should guide dose selection and adjustment?
o: Select a target dose from the usual range despite troublesome adverse effects
Start at the full target dose and escalate rapidly for inadequate response
Adjust the dose to individual response, adverse effects, safety, and drug interactions
Set the effective dose from age and weight before assessing treatment response
explanation:
**Antidepressant dosing** is individualized rather than fixed by a universal therapeutic window (p. 1015). Hazzard states: "the best dosage is not a number fixed in stone, but rather the dosage that works for that individual patient" and "Safety, side effects, and interactions will dictate the maximum dosage" (p. 1015). It also favors slow titration rather than beginning at a full dose (p. 1015).

**A. Select a target dose from the usual range despite troublesome adverse effects.** Wrong, the source makes side effects and safety limits part of dose selection. Persisting toward a generic target despite troublesome effects disregards those limits (p. 1015).
**B. Start at the full target dose and escalate rapidly for inadequate response.** Wrong, the source recommends planning slow upward titration rather than starting at a full dosage. A full-dose start with rapid escalation does not follow that approach (p. 1015).
**C. Adjust the dose to individual response, adverse effects, safety, and drug interactions.** Correct, this combines the individual response with the factors that limit dosage in the source. It does not presume that a particular dose is effective or tolerable for every patient (p. 1015).
**D. Set the effective dose from age and weight before assessing treatment response.** Wrong, the source defines the best dosage by what works for the individual and by safety, adverse effects, and interactions. Age and weight without response assessment do not supply that individualized judgment (p. 1015).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1015.

q: A 77-year-old man with falls takes recently initiated citalopram. After assessment, the team decides that a trial of discontinuation is appropriate. Which principle should guide this change?
o: Stop abruptly and monitor for improved walking and sleep
Stop abruptly and immediately substitute another medication
Taper gradually and clinically reassess symptoms during withdrawal
Continue the current treatment without reassessing its benefit
explanation:
**Antidepressant discontinuation** should allow time for tapering and symptom assessment. The source advises considering whether symptoms during withdrawal reflect withdrawal itself, lack of efficacy, or natural fluctuation (p. 1016).
"Allow time to taper off the medication." (p. 1016).
"Continue to assess symptoms during withdrawal, and question whether symptoms can be attributed to withdrawal, lack of efficacy, or natural fluctuation." (p. 1016).

**A. Stop abruptly and monitor for improved walking and sleep.** Wrong, abrupt cessation omits the recommended time for tapering; monitoring walking and sleep does not replace assessment during withdrawal (p. 1016).
**B. Stop abruptly and immediately substitute another medication.** Wrong, immediate abrupt substitution omits the recommended tapering interval and symptom reassessment (p. 1016).
**C. Taper gradually and clinically reassess symptoms during withdrawal.** Correct, this combines the source’s tapering and ongoing assessment recommendations (p. 1016).
**D. Continue the current treatment without reassessing its benefit.** Wrong, the source calls for reassessment of benefit at each appointment, not continuation without review (p. 1016).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1016.

q: A 79-year-old woman has functional decline, cognitive complaints, and significant depressive symptoms after a mild head injury. Which principle should guide assessment and treatment?
o: Integrate depression assessment with cognition and function in this complex presentation
Attribute functional decline to the injury and assess depression after rehabilitation
Attribute cognitive decline to the injury and assess mood on a separate pathway
Focus assessment on memory and postpone review of daily functional decline
explanation:
**Late-life depression** is associated with disability and cognitive impairment, so it belongs in an integrated assessment. Its relationship with impaired health and function is described as bidirectional; the source does not establish that the injury alone explains this patient's decline (p. 1008). "It is associated with disability, cognitive impairment, perception of poorer health and quality of life" (p. 1008).

**A. Integrate depression assessment with cognition and function in this complex presentation.** Correct, integrating these domains reflects the described relationship between depression, cognition, and function (p. 1008).
**B. Attribute functional decline to the injury and assess depression after rehabilitation.** Wrong, deferring depression assessment overlooks its described relationship with disability in the current presentation (p. 1008).
**C. Attribute cognitive decline to the injury and assess mood on a separate pathway.** Wrong, separating mood from cognitive assessment overlooks the source's association between depression and cognitive impairment (p. 1008).
**D. Focus assessment on memory and postpone review of daily functional decline.** Wrong, postponing functional assessment neglects an important domain associated with depression and its interaction with health (p. 1008).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1008.

q: After shared discussion, an older woman whose condition is stable begins a gradual venlafaxine taper. New symptoms appear during dose reduction. How should they be interpreted?
o: Consider depressive relapse and resume long-term treatment on that basis
Consider drug inefficacy and change the medication on that basis
Consider withdrawal, inefficacy or fluctuation and reassess symptoms
Consider an effect of aging and continue the taper on that basis
explanation:
**Symptoms during antidepressant withdrawal** require reassessment because withdrawal can be confused with lack of efficacy or recurrence. The chapter recommends continuing symptom assessment and considering withdrawal, lack of efficacy and natural fluctuation instead of assigning a cause from timing alone (p. 1016).
"Continue to assess symptoms during withdrawal, and question whether symptoms can be attributed to withdrawal, lack of efficacy, or natural fluctuation." (p. 1016).

**A. Consider depressive relapse and resume long-term treatment on that basis.** Wrong, the source warns that withdrawal symptoms can be mistaken for relapse; recurrence should be distinguished from discontinuation effects before deciding on long-term treatment (p. 1016).
**B. Consider drug inefficacy and change the medication on that basis.** Wrong, lack of efficacy is one possibility to assess, but withdrawal and natural fluctuation must also be considered (p. 1016).
**C. Consider withdrawal, inefficacy or fluctuation and reassess symptoms.** Correct, this follows the chapter's explicit approach to monitoring and interpreting symptoms during withdrawal (p. 1016).
**D. Consider an effect of aging and continue the taper on that basis.** Wrong, attributing symptoms to aging bypasses the recommended reassessment of withdrawal, efficacy and natural fluctuation (p. 1016).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1016.

q: An 82-year-old man with mild dementia and treated depression has acquired a firearm for protection. His wife recently found him looking sad while holding the loaded gun. He denies suicidal thoughts and says he was checking the weapon. He takes sertraline and donepezil. Alongside immediate assessment of suicide risk, which action directly reduces access to lethal means?
o: Increase the antidepressant dose and arrange a later follow-up visit
Arrange a mental-health referral while leaving firearm access unchanged
Document firearm-storage advice while leaving firearm access unchanged
Work with family to remove access to the firearm temporarily
explanation:
**Reducing access to lethal means** is an immediate risk-reduction measure, alongside assessment of intent, planning, and available means. Hazzard states that "removing the firearm or other means can decrease immediate risk" (p. 1018). It describes involving someone in the patient’s life to help decrease access; applying that principle here does not establish intent or rule out the need for hospitalization.

**A. Increase the antidepressant dose and arrange a later follow-up visit.** Wrong, a dose change and later review do not reduce the immediate availability of the firearm, the specific risk addressed by the source passage (p. 1018).
**B. Arrange a mental-health referral while leaving firearm access unchanged.** Wrong, specialist referral may be needed, but leaving the weapon accessible does not implement the immediate means-reduction measure (p. 1018).
**C. Document firearm-storage advice while leaving firearm access unchanged.** Wrong, documentation and advice do not accomplish removal of access if the firearm remains available (p. 1018; application).
**D. Work with family to remove access to the firearm temporarily.** Correct, this enlists support to reduce actual access while the clinical risk assessment and further care proceed (p. 1018).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1018.

q: An 83-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension improved after escitalopram treatment for major depression. She now reports falls and cognitive symptoms, and medication review raises concern about adverse effects. After reassessing benefits and risks, she and her clinician decide to discontinue treatment without an emergency indication for abrupt cessation. Which follow-up plan follows Hazzard?
o: Maintain the current prescription and defer further review of benefit
Stop treatment abruptly and classify new symptoms as depressive relapse
Taper treatment and defer symptom assessment until withdrawal is complete
Taper treatment and monitor symptoms during and after withdrawal
explanation:
**Antidepressant discontinuation** needs ongoing assessment because withdrawal can resemble recurrence. Hazzard recommends: "Allow time to taper off the medication." and "Continue to assess symptoms during withdrawal" (p. 1016). New symptoms should be considered in relation to withdrawal, lack of efficacy, and natural fluctuation rather than automatically labeled relapse.

**A. Maintain the current prescription and defer further review of benefit.** Wrong, this does not implement the agreed discontinuation and conflicts with reassessing benefit at each appointment (p. 1016).
**B. Stop treatment abruptly and classify new symptoms as depressive relapse.** Wrong, the source recommends allowing time for tapering and distinguishing withdrawal symptoms from relapse rather than assuming recurrence (p. 1016).
**C. Taper treatment and defer symptom assessment until withdrawal is complete.** Wrong, monitoring is recommended during withdrawal, so waiting until it is complete misses the period specifically identified in the guidance (p. 1016).
**D. Taper treatment and monitor symptoms during and after withdrawal.** Correct, this follows deliberate discontinuation with symptom monitoring and attention to the possible explanations for new symptoms (p. 1016).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1016.

q: A 72-year-old woman has severe depression, reduced food intake and function, and limited response to several medication trials. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is being considered. Which information is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Older adults tend to respond less well than younger patients
Trials have found medication more effective than this treatment
Its initial benefits remain durable without maintenance treatment
It warrants early consideration after limited medication response
explanation:
**ECT** should be considered early for severe or psychotic depression and when medication response has been limited. Hazzard describes strong efficacy in older adults but notes that benefits can diminish over time and maintenance treatment is sometimes needed (p. 1014).
"ECT should be considered as an early option for patients with severe or psychotic depression, and for those who have had limited medication response." (p. 1014).
"No trial has ever found medications to be more effective than ECT." (p. 1014).

**A. Older adults tend to respond less well than younger patients.** Wrong, older patients are described as appearing even more responsive than younger adults (p. 1014).
**B. Trials have found medication more effective than this treatment.** Wrong, the source states that no trial has found medication more effective than ECT (p. 1014).
**C. Its initial benefits remain durable without maintenance treatment.** Wrong, benefits can decay over time, and maintenance ECT is sometimes required (p. 1014).
**D. It warrants early consideration after limited medication response.** Correct, severe illness and limited response to medication are the situations named for early consideration (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1014.

q: A 78-year-old man is diagnosed with major depression. After discussion, he chooses medication, and sertraline is selected. Which principle for initiation and follow-up agrees with Hazzard?
o: Start at a low dose, titrate to response, and ask about adverse effects
Start at the intended target dose to obtain better adherence from the outset
Choose a uniform target dose and assess response after reaching it
Wait for spontaneous reports and infer tolerability from a lack of complaints
explanation:
**Antidepressant dosing** should be individualized: Hazzard describes better adherence with lower starting doses followed by titration. **Tolerability** must be asked about directly, since patients may not volunteer adverse effects and may instead stop treatment (p. 1015). "the best dosage is not a number fixed in stone, but rather the dosage that works for that individual patient." (p. 1015).

**A. Start at a low dose, titrate to response, and ask about adverse effects.** Correct, this combines gradual initiation, individual response-based dosing, and active adverse-effect inquiry (p. 1015).
**B. Start at the intended target dose to obtain better adherence from the outset.** Wrong, the described adherence advantage occurred with lower initial dosing and titration rather than a higher starting dose (p. 1015).
**C. Choose a uniform target dose and assess response after reaching it.** Wrong, the source says the appropriate dose is the one that works for the individual, not a universal fixed target (p. 1015).
**D. Wait for spontaneous reports and infer tolerability from a lack of complaints.** Wrong, patients may be reluctant to report side effects unless asked, so silence does not establish tolerability (p. 1015).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1015.

q: An 83-year-old woman in rehabilitation after a hip fracture cries, eats little, and says she wants to die. Her evaluation is not yet complete. What should be included immediately in suicide-risk assessment?
o: Suicidal thoughts, intent, plans, and access to means
Appetite, weight, sleep habits, and daily protein intake
Pain, range of motion, strength, and rehabilitation participation
Memory, orientation, daily function, and family dependence
explanation:
**Suicide-risk assessment** requires direct exploration of thoughts and the possibility of acting on them. Hazzard states that assessment should include “suicidal thoughts, intent to act on suicidal thoughts, suicidal plans, and access to lethal means” (p. 1008). The expressed wish to die makes these domains the focus of the question; the stem does not yet establish a diagnosis of major depression.

**A. Suicidal thoughts, intent, plans, and access to means.** Correct, all four domains are explicitly included in the source’s minimum suicide-risk assessment (p. 1008).
**B. Appetite, weight, sleep habits, and daily protein intake.** Wrong, these domains may belong to a broader assessment, but they do not assess suicidal intent, planning, or access to means (p. 1008).
**C. Pain, range of motion, strength, and rehabilitation participation.** Wrong, functional rehabilitation measures do not replace direct assessment of suicidal thoughts and potential action (p. 1008).
**D. Memory, orientation, daily function, and family dependence.** Wrong, cognition and dependency measures do not provide the source’s minimum information about suicidal intent, plans, and means (p. 1008).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1008.

q: A 72-year-old man with severe depression has not improved after adequate medication trials. Electroconvulsive therapy is being considered. Which statement matches Hazzard’s explanation of treatment?
o: Consider delaying ECT because older patients respond poorly
Consider ECT for severe depression with limited medication response
Consider continuing medication because trials show greater efficacy than ECT
Consider ECT with the expectation that its benefit will not decline
explanation:
**Electroconvulsive therapy** is an option for severe depression and limited medication response. Hazzard describes older patients as particularly responsive, but also notes that benefit tends to decline over time and maintenance ECT is sometimes required. (p. 1014)
"ECT should be considered as an early option for patients with severe or psychotic depression, and for those who have had limited medication response." (p. 1014)
"Older patients seem to be even more responsive to ECT than younger adults." (p. 1014)

**A. Consider delaying ECT because older patients respond poorly.** Wrong, older patients are described as more responsive than younger adults, so poor response due to age is not the reason given for delay. (p. 1014)
**B. Consider ECT for severe depression with limited medication response.** Correct, severe depression and limited medication response are both situations in which the source recommends considering ECT. (p. 1014)
**C. Consider continuing medication because trials show greater efficacy than ECT.** Wrong, the source states that no trial found medication more effective than ECT, so this proposed comparative justification is unsupported. (p. 1014)
**D. Consider ECT with the expectation that its benefit will not decline.** Wrong, beneficial effects tend to decay over time, and maintenance ECT is sometimes required. (p. 1014)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1014.

q: A 78-year-old man with metastatic cancer and uncontrolled pain says that he wants to die and that he has a gun. A suicidal plan and intent have not yet been assessed. Which action is needed now alongside treatment of his suffering?
o: Adjust analgesia and revisit the statement at the next appointment
Start an antidepressant and reassess after its therapeutic effect
Assess a suicide plan and reduce access to the firearm
Discuss treatment goals and arrange routine outpatient follow-up
explanation:
**Suicidal statements** require assessment of a plan and access to means. Hazzard emphasizes that removing a firearm or other means can decrease immediate risk; treating pain does not replace that immediate assessment (pp. 1017-1018; application).
"It is most important to assess whether a patient expressing suicidal ideation has started to develop a plan or has one already formulated." (p. 1018).

**A. Adjust analgesia and revisit the statement at the next appointment.** Wrong, deferral leaves the unassessed plan and available means unresolved despite the immediate-risk assessment described in the source (p. 1018).
**B. Start an antidepressant and reassess after its therapeutic effect.** Wrong, waiting for an antidepressant effect does not assess the plan or reduce present access to means (p. 1018; application).
**C. Assess a suicide plan and reduce access to the firearm.** Correct, this addresses the two immediate issues highlighted: a possible plan and access to a firearm (p. 1018).
**D. Discuss treatment goals and arrange routine outpatient follow-up.** Wrong, goals discussion and routine follow-up do not by themselves complete the required suicide-risk assessment (p. 1018; application).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1018, 1017.

q: An older woman with COPD and depression is being followed clinically. Which suicide-risk assessment is required as part of evaluating her depression?
o: Mood, sleep quality, appetite, and daily energy
Thoughts, intent, plans, and daily respiratory function
Thoughts, intent, plans, and access to lethal means
Past attempts, sleep quality, appetite, and family support
explanation:
**Suicide-risk assessment** is required for depressed older patients (p. 1008). At minimum it includes "suicidal thoughts, intent to act on suicidal thoughts, suicidal plans, and access to lethal means" (p. 1008).

**A. Mood, sleep quality, appetite, and daily energy.** Wrong, mood and somatic symptoms do not cover the required thoughts, intent, plans, and access to means (p. 1008).
**B. Thoughts, intent, plans, and daily respiratory function.** Wrong, respiratory function does not replace the required assessment of access to lethal means (p. 1008).
**C. Thoughts, intent, plans, and access to lethal means.** Correct, this set includes all the minimum components specified in the source (p. 1008).
**D. Past attempts, sleep quality, appetite, and family support.** Wrong, past attempts and support do not replace current thoughts, intent, plans, and access to means (p. 1008).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1008.

q: בן 78, מהנדס במקצוע, בגמלאות, אלמן כשלושה חודשים, הילדים תומכים בו, מתגורר. לבד בבית פרטי. הגיע לייעוץ עקב ירידה קוגניטיבית. הוא דיווח שבחודשיים האחרונים הוא מרגיש ירידה בזיכרון טווח קצר – שוכח איפה שם חפצים, שואל שוב ושוב את אותה שאלה. בנוסף מתקשה להת. רכז בקריאה או בטלוויזיה ברקע: סוכרת, יתר לחץ דם ויתר שומנים בדם, מ/א אירוע מוחי איסכמי קל ללא חסרים. נוירולוגיים. מאוזן מבחינת מחלות הרקע תחת טיפול תרופתי. מבחן MMSE - תמונה מספר 3 עברה שנה והמטופל הגיע למרפאה למעקב. בדיקת MMSE היתה 28/30. איזה טיפול סביר שקיבל?
o: מעכבי אצטיל כולין
נוגדי דיכאון
קנאביס רפואי
תרגול קוגניטיבי
explanation:
Official answer: ב

**Late-life depression** can involve difficulty concentrating and cognitive impairment, so bereavement with memory complaints requires mood assessment (p. 1008). Inference in this question: antidepressants are the official answer, but improvement in MMSE alone neither proves the treatment received nor excludes cognitive disease; screening scores can be normal even in dementia (pp. 873, 1015).
"It is associated with disability, cognitive impairment" (p. 1008).

**A. Acetylcholine inhibitors.** Wrong, if acetylcholinesterase inhibitors are intended, the source describes modest delay of Alzheimer symptoms, not evidence that by itself explains this improvement after bereavement. This is an inference within the question, not retrospective proof that they were not given (p. 911).
**B. Antidepressants.** Correct, officially accepted. The source supports the association between depression and cognitive impairment and antidepressant treatment for major depression. Depression must be diagnosed, not inferred from bereavement or MMSE alone (pp. 1008, 1015).
**C. Medical cannabis.** Wrong, not officially accepted; the checked treatment discussion provides no basis for attributing the improvement to cannabis as depression treatment. It discusses psychotherapy and antidepressants according to diagnosis (pp. 1014–1015).
**D. Cognitive training.** Wrong, not officially accepted. Cognitive training is not the same as the psychotherapy for depression described in the source, and the follow-up score alone cannot attribute improvement to it. This is an inference in the question, not a general denial of its value (pp. 1014–1015).

Note: The stem contains broken punctuation within the descriptions of living alone, difficulty concentrating and absence of neurologic deficits. “Acetylcholine inhibitors” is not the precise name of acetylcholinesterase inhibitors. The follow-up score does not establish with certainty which treatment was given.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 873, 911, 1008, 1014, 1015.

q: איזו מבין התרופות נוגדות דיכאון הבאות עשויה לגרום להפרעת הקצב באק"ג בתמונה מספר 8?
o: Citralopam ( ציפרמיל)
Duloxetine ( סימבלטה)
Bupropion Hydrobromide (וולבוטרין)
Hypericum perforatum ( רמוטיב)
explanation:
The tracing shows polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, consistent in this question with **torsades de pointes**. Citalopram is associated with QT prolongation, and the review distinguishes it from duloxetine and bupropion at the therapeutic doses studied. This does not imply that the other drugs have no cardiac risk (Aronow and Shamliyan, Citalopram, Bupropion, and Duloxetine sections; attached image).

**A. Citalopram (Cipramil).** Correct, the QT-prolongation association is supported by Hazzard and the review and fits the pattern being tested (pp. 929-930; Aronow and Shamliyan).
**B. Duloxetine (Cymbalta).** Wrong, the summarized evidence did not show QT prolongation at the doses studied, although evidence quality is limited. It therefore does not share the same established association here; this is not a guarantee of no risk in every situation (Aronow and Shamliyan, Duloxetine).
**C. Bupropion hydrobromide (Wellbutrin).** Wrong, the review found no association with QT prolongation at the therapeutic doses examined. That conclusion does not cover overdose or unstudied circumstances (Aronow and Shamliyan, Bupropion).
**D. Hypericum perforatum (Remotiv).** Wrong, according to the official key, but it should not be taught as incapable of prolonging QT: a case report describes QT prolongation and ventricular premature complexes after its use. This limited report does not establish the same arrhythmia shown in the image or risk equivalent to citalopram (Özkan et al., Abstract).

Citalopram is associated with QT prolongation. The image is consistent with torsades de pointes, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in the setting of prolonged QT; the source does not support the wording "especially escitalopram" (Hazzard 8e, pp. 929-930; inherited Harrison 22e locator: p. 1969, Figure 262-1B).

Note: QT prolongation, ventricular premature complexes, and torsades de pointes are different outcomes, and evidence levels differ between drugs.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 929-930; Aronow WS, Shamliyan TA. Effects of antidepressants on QT interval in people with mental disorders. Arch Med Sci. 2020;16:727-741. doi:10.5114/aoms.2019.86928, drug-specific sections; Özkan H et al. A Rare Cardiac Side Effect of a Herbal Medicine; QT Prolongation Due to Hypericum Perforatum: Case Report. Turkiye Klinikleri J Case Rep. 2014;22:139-141, Abstract; https://www.turkiyeklinikleri.com/article/en-a-rare-cardiac-side-effect-of-a-herbal-medicine-qt-prolongation-due-to-hypericum-perforatum-case-report-69051.html.

q: בת 89, בעלת תואר שני במדעים. פנתה לבירור בשל תלונות על מצב רוח ירוד, תחושת ריקנות, בדידות ועיסוק רב במחשבות על בעלה שנפטר לפני כשבועיים בהיותו מאושפז על. רקע דלקת ראות מה מהבאים מהווה גורם סיכון להתפתחות Persistent complex bereavement disorder בקרב המטופלת?
o: השכלתה האקדמית
היותה אישה
היעדר רקע של הפרעת חרדה או דכאון
מותו של בעלה לאחר מחלה ממושכת
explanation:
**Female sex** is associated with increased risk of prolonged grief symptoms. This is a statistical association, not a basis for inventing a mechanism involving emotional dependence or a female coping style (Buur et al., 2024, Abstract). **Grief two weeks after a loss is not itself prolonged grief disorder**; the question concerns future risk, not a present diagnosis (Hazzard 8e, p. 80).

**A. Her academic education.** Wrong, the meta-analysis found an association with lower education; a master's degree is not the risk characteristic sought here (Buur et al., Abstract).
**B. Being a woman.** Correct, female sex was among the factors associated with prolonged grief symptoms (Buur et al., Abstract).
**C. No history of anxiety or depression.** Wrong, a history of mood disorder and depression around bereavement are associated with increased risk; their absence is not that risk factor (Szuhany et al., Grief Course and Risk Factors).
**D. Her husband's death after prolonged illness.** Wrong, as the distinguishing characteristic among these choices: the meta-analysis describes risk associated with unexpected or violent death. This does not exclude prolonged grief after illness, but illness duration itself should not be turned into the established risk factor in this question (Buur et al., Abstract).

Missing step: The source defines persistent complex bereavement disorder as a trauma- or stress-related condition lasting 6 or 12 months after death and states that 9%-25% of older adults develop persistent or complicated grief (Hazzard 8e, p. 80), but does not list risk factors. Thus, explanations for academic education, absence of prior anxiety or depression, and death after prolonged illness were missing from the sources then in hand.
Source completion: The protected note describes the limits of Hazzard's support; the checked external sources complete the risk-factor comparison (Buur et al., Abstract; Szuhany et al., Grief Course and Risk Factors).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 80; Buur et al. Clin Psychol Rev. 2024;107:102375, Abstract, doi:10.1016/j.cpr.2023.102375; Szuhany et al. Focus. 2021;19:161-172, Grief Course and Risk Factors, doi:10.1176/appi.focus.20200052.

q: בן 75, מאובחן עם דיכאון. מזה שבועיים מקבל טיפול של ESCITALOPRAM במינון 5 מ"ג. מדווח על שיפור מסוים במצב הרוח, אך עדיין מתקשה בשינה ומרגיש חוסר אנרגיה. מה נכון להמליץ במצב זה?
o: להחליף טיפול ל- MIRTAZAPINE במינון 15 מ"ג
להמשיך טיפול ב- ESCITALOPRAM במינון 5 מ"ג והוסיף MIRTAZAPINE במינון 15 מ"ג
להוסיף טיפול ב- QUETIAPINE במינון 12.5 מ"ג
להעלות מינון ESCITALOPRAM ל- 10 מ"ג
explanation:
**Partial improvement after only two weeks** is too early to establish treatment failure. The source supports starting at a low dose and titrating to individual response and tolerability; the inference here is to optimize the existing treatment before switching or adding another drug (pp. 1014–1015). Sleep and energy may still improve over subsequent weeks; assess tolerability and response after increasing the dose (pp. 1014–1015).

**A. Switch to mirtazapine 15 mg.** Wrong, with partial improvement and a short trial, failure has not been adequately established. An immediate switch bypasses time to assess response and titration of the existing drug; this is an inference from the treatment principles (pp. 1014–1015).
**B. Continue escitalopram 5 mg and add mirtazapine 15 mg.** Wrong, adding another drug does not address the inadequate duration of the first trial. Inference: low-dose initiation and individualized titration favor optimizing the initial treatment (pp. 1014–1015).
**C. Add quetiapine 12.5 mg.** Wrong, early insomnia and partial improvement do not establish treatment failure that justifies bypassing optimization of the first drug; this is an inference from the treatment approach (pp. 1014–1015).
**D. Increase escitalopram to 10 mg.** Correct, the officially accepted step optimizes current treatment after partial response, with assessment of tolerability and benefit. The drug table lists 5 mg initially and 10 mg as the maximum daily dose (pp. 929, 1014–1015).

Switching to mirtazapine: the reasoning is an inference from the treatment principles on pp. 1014–1015.
Adding mirtazapine: the reasoning is an inference from pp. 1014–1015.
Adding quetiapine: the reasoning is an inference from the stepwise approach on pp. 1014–1015.

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 929, 1014, 1015.

q: מה מתאר את הקשר בין דיכאון לשבר בצוואר הירך?
o: הדיכאון נמשך בדרך כלל כשנה אחרי השבר
אין קשר בן קיום דיכאון למצב התפקודי
דיכאון הוא אחד הגורמים המאטים את קצב השיקום
היות ומדובר בדיכאון תגובתי לא מומלץ לתת טיפול תרופתי
explanation:
**Depressive symptoms after hip fracture** are associated with poorer functional recovery. They should be assessed as part of rehabilitation and treated according to severity (Hazzard 8e, pp. 799–801, 1011).

**A. Depression usually lasts about a year after the fracture.** Wrong, there is no fixed one-year duration: the source says symptoms frequently resolve within two months with limited intervention (p. 801).
**B. Depression is unrelated to functional status.** Wrong, even transient depressive symptoms are associated with poorer recovery, so mood and function should not be separated (p. 799).
**C. Depression is one factor that slows rehabilitation.** Correct, depression is explicitly among the factors to assess when recovery is slower than expected, so that a targeted treatment plan can be developed (p. 800).
**D. Because the depression is reactive, drug treatment is not recommended.** Wrong, its occurrence after a fracture does not rule out treatment. The source describes benefit from treating postfracture depression, and antidepressants with or without psychotherapy for severe depression (pp. 801, 1011).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 799–801, 1011.

q: בן 78, אובחן עם דיכאון מג'ורי לראשונה בחייו. ברקע אי ספיקת לב (NYHA II), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), יתר לחץ דם, נוירופתיה והגדלה שפירה של הערמונית. מה מהבאים נכון באשר לשיקולים לבחירת טיפול תרופתי?
o: יש עדיפות למתן Citalopram על פני Paroxetine בשל הסיכון להשפעה אנטיכולינרגית
יש עדיפות למתן Mirtazapine על פני Bupropion (Wellbutrin) בשל הסיכון לפגיעה בתפקוד המיני
יש עדיפות למתן Citalopram על פני Escitalopram בשל הסיכון להיפונתרמיה
יש עדיפות למתן Citalopram על פני Mirtazapine בשל הסיכון לאריתמיה
explanation:
**Anticholinergic burden** matters in a patient with cognitive impairment. Paroxetine has anticholinergic properties and should be avoided in older adults. Choosing citalopram, however, does not eliminate hyponatremia or QT-prolongation risks; selection must reflect the whole clinical picture (pp. 929-930).
"Some SSRIs, such as paroxetine, have anticholinergic properties and should be avoided in older adults." (p. 930).

**A. Prefer citalopram to paroxetine because of anticholinergic effects.** Correct, paroxetine adds anticholinergic burden that may increase delirium risk, a relevant concern here (pp. 929-930).
**B. Prefer mirtazapine to bupropion because of sexual dysfunction.** Wrong, both are lower-risk alternatives for sexual adverse effects, and bupropion's incidence is described as similar to placebo. This rationale does not establish a blanket preference for mirtazapine (Montejo et al., Switching to Bupropion and Switching to Mirtazapine).
**C. Prefer citalopram to escitalopram because of hyponatremia.** Wrong, hyponatremia and SIADH are listed for both. Switching between them neither eliminates this risk nor establishes the proposed preference (p. 929).
**D. Prefer citalopram to mirtazapine because of arrhythmia.** Wrong, citalopram itself is associated with QT prolongation, and mirtazapine also requires attention to QT. The book does not establish citalopram as the safer electrical-risk choice (p. 929).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 929-930, Table 60-9; Montejo AL et al. Management Strategies for Antidepressant-Related Sexual Dysfunction: A Clinical Approach. J Clin Med. 2019;8:1640. doi:10.3390/jcm8101640, treatment-switching sections.

q: בן 84, סובל מדמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר מזה שנתיים. פנה למרפאה עקב ירידה. תפקודית לדברי המשפחה הוא ממעט לצאת מהבית ומסתובב בבית באי שקט. לעיתים בוכה במשך היום ומתרגז על דברים קטנים. הוא ישן הרבה ומסרב לצאת מהמיטה. בשיחה - מתקשה לבטא מה מפריע לו, אך פורץ בבכי במהלך השי. חה כשנשאל על הקשר עם משפחתו אומדנים- MMSE - 22/30, PHQ2 - 5/6. מה הטיפול התרופתי המומלץ בשלב ראשון?
o: ESCITALOPRAM
DONEPEZIL
VENLAFAXINE
MIRTAZAPINE
explanation:
**Official answer: א, ב** (IMA, final official answer key after appeals, 2023-Jun, question 7).

Hazzard 8e, the examination textbook, discusses **SSRIs for late-life depression**, with limited evidence in depression accompanying dementia; donepezil treats Alzheimer symptoms. These are different treatment aims (p. 929; Table 59-7, p. 912).

**A. Escitalopram.** Correct, for official scoring. It is an SSRI, a first-line class for late-life depression, with the limited evidence in dementia qualified above (p. 929).
**B. Donepezil.** Correct, for official scoring. It treats Alzheimer symptoms; acceptance in the key does not establish it as an antidepressant (p. 912, Table 59-7).
**C. Venlafaxine.** Wrong, not officially accepted. It is used in late-life depression, but the cited dementia studies did not show a significant depressive-symptom benefit, providing no basis here to prefer it first (p. 930).
**D. Mirtazapine.** Wrong, not officially accepted. The described trial did not show superiority to placebo for depression in dementia; increased daytime sleepiness is also relevant to the patient's existing somnolence (p. 930).

Current guidance/consensus comparison, secondary source: The examination's 2024 review emphasizes investigating causes and tailored nonpharmacologic interventions for behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia. Psychotropic efficacy evidence is limited and there are risks. This does not replace individualized assessment and treatment of clinical depression (Reuben, Kremen and Maust, JAMA Internal Medicine 2024, online p. E6, Treatment of Behavioral and Psychological Complications).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 912, 929-930; Reuben DB, Kremen S, Maust DT. Dementia Prevention and Treatment: A Narrative Review. JAMA Intern Med. 2024;184:563-572, online p. E6. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2023.8522

הפרעות בשינה

הטיפול בבעלה הסיעודי

q: בן 74. מזה כחודשיים תסמיני דיכאון המשפיעים על התפקוד היומיומי. נבדק במרפאה ובוצע PHQ9. מצ"ב תמונת התוצאה של המבחן (ראה תמונה מספר 3). לפי הממצאים מהי האבחנה המתאימה?
o: Major Depression
Minor Depression
דיסתימיה
ללא דיכאון.
explanation:
**Official answer:** Minor depression; No depression (IMA, final answer key, May 2024 examination, question 16).

Image 3 marks three symptoms as occurring on "several days" only, with the others marked "not at all." The source's PHQ-9 instructions count symptoms occurring on more than half the days or nearly every day, with a separate exception for item 9. None of the marked symptoms therefore enters the diagnostic count; a severity score of 3 and functional difficulty do not supply the 2-4 qualifying symptoms required for minor depression. The official key accepts minor depression as well as "no depression" (Hazzard 8e, p. 1011, Figure 65-2; IMA May 2024 album, PDF p. 4).

**A. Major depression.** Wrong, the photographed questionnaire does not show the required number of symptoms at diagnostic frequency; functional difficulty alone does not meet this requirement (p. 1011).
**B. Minor depression.** Correct, for scoring because it was officially accepted; clinical support is limited for the reason stated in the source note above (p. 1011; album, PDF p. 4).
**C. Dysthymia.** Wrong, the source describes chronic depression lasting two years. The scenario describes only two months, and the questionnaire's symptom requirements are also unmet (p. 1011).
**D. No depression.** Correct, officially accepted and consistent with the absence of symptoms at diagnostic frequency on the form. This does not exclude distress or a need for clinical assessment (p. 1011; album, PDF p. 4).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1011; IMA May 2024 album, PDF p. 4.

q: איזה מידע תוכל לתת למטופל ומשפחתו בנוגע לטיפול בנזעי חשמל (ECT)?
o: מדובר בטיפול חד פעמי
קיימת פגיעה בזיכרון לטווח קצר שאינה הפיכה
ביותר ממחצית המטופלים צפויה הפוגה (רמיסיה)
קשישים יגיבו פחות טוב לנזעי חשמל ביחס לצעירים
explanation:
**Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)** is particularly effective for depression, and older patients can respond well (Hazzard 8e, p. 1014).

**A. It is a one-time treatment.** Wrong, ECT is delivered as a course rather than a single procedure; maintenance treatment is sometimes needed as the benefit of the course wanes (p. 1014).
**B. It causes irreversible short-term memory impairment.** Wrong, short-term memory loss almost always resolves within weeks after the course, so it should not generally be described as irreversible damage (p. 1014).
**C. More than half of patients are expected to achieve remission.** Correct, the source reports remission rates over 60% in most studies, supporting remission in more than half (p. 1014).
**D. Older adults respond less well than younger adults.** Wrong, the source says older patients seem even more responsive than younger adults (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1014.

q: איזה מבין ההיגדים הבאים נכון באשר ליעילות הטיפול התרופתי בדיכאון בזקנים?
o: יעילות הטיפול התרופתי בחולים הלוקים בדמנציה מוטלת בספק
יעילות הטיפול בפלצבו זניחה בקרב מטופלים זקנים
יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר בקרב המאובחנים עם דיכאון קל לעומת דיכאון חמור
יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר ככל שהטיטרציה במינון מהירה יותר
explanation:
In patients with **dementia and depression**, antidepressant benefit is questionable after many negative trials. Assess measurable benefit rather than continuing treatment simply because it has already been prescribed (p. 1015).

**A. Drug-treatment efficacy in patients with dementia is questionable.** Correct, the source summarizes this conclusion after many negative studies (p. 1015).
**B. Placebo efficacy is negligible in older patients.** Wrong, placebo responses can be substantial, especially in less severe depression (p. 1014).
**C. Drug treatment is more effective in mild than severe depression.** Wrong, there is no evidence of benefit in mild or subthreshold depression; benefit beyond placebo is described mainly in more severe cases (pp. 1014-1015).
**D. Faster dose titration improves drug-treatment efficacy.** Wrong, starting low and titrating gradually was associated with better adherence even at the same eventual dose. The source proposes fewer adverse effects and more individualized attention as possible explanations, rather than an advantage from faster titration (p. 1015).

Gradual titration's association with adherence does not mean reaching the target faster guarantees greater efficacy (p. 1015). The placebo effect may be substantial, especially in less severe depression; the page does not provide the numerical range stated in an earlier explanation (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014-1015.

q: בן 68, ברקע מחלת לב אסכמית, הגדלה שפירה של הערמונית וגלאוקומה. אובחן לאחרונה עם סרטן שלפוחית השתן. סובל מדיכאון, ללא הפרעת שינה והתיאבון שמור. בבדיקות מעבדה: תפקודי כבד תקינים, רמות ויטמין B12, סידן ותפקודי תריס תקינים. מהו קו הטיפול הראשון לדיכאון במטופל זה?
o: SSRI's
SNRI’s
TCA's
MAO-I
explanation:
**SSRIs** are an appropriate first-line option here, with drug selection and adverse-effect monitoring tailored to the patient. Paroxetine has anticholinergic activity and should be avoided in older adults (pp. 929–930, 1392). The cancer chapter particularly favors SSRIs with ischemic heart disease or conduction defects, prostatic hypertrophy, or uncontrolled glaucoma; it lists venlafaxine, mirtazapine, and bupropion as second-line drugs (p. 1392).

**A. SSRIs.** Correct, they are the source's first-line choice, particularly with the cardiac and anticholinergic concerns represented in this patient's comorbidities; individual drug selection still matters (pp. 929–930, 1392).
**B. SNRIs.** Wrong, venlafaxine is listed as second-line in this context, and venlafaxine and desvenlafaxine can cause dose-dependent hypertension, a concern in this patient with ischemic heart disease (pp. 929, 1392; application to the case).
**C. TCAs.** Wrong, nortriptyline and desipramine are listed as third-line and can be difficult to tolerate; anticholinergic effects and hypotension are particularly concerning with the comorbidities for which the source favors SSRIs (pp. 929, 1392).
**D. MAO inhibitors.** Wrong, use is limited by a low-tyramine diet, serotonin-syndrome risk with serotonergic drugs, and dietary and medication restrictions (pp. 930, 1392).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 929–930, 1392.

q: בת 82 אלמנה ואם ל-2, עצמאית ופעילה, דיירת דיור מוגן פנתה למרפאה עקב ירידה במצב הרוח ובאנרגיה. הוחלט להתחיל טיפול בנוגדי דיכאון. מה תופעת לוואי משמעותית של תרופות נוגדות דיכאון באישה זו?
o: דליריום משני לטיפול ב- Paroxetine
הארכת QT ו- Torsades de Pointes משנית ל- Venlafaxine
Orthostatic Hypotension משני לטיפול ב- Bupropion
Serotonin Syndrome משני לטיפול ב- Citalopram
explanation:
**Official answers:** delirium due to paroxetine; serotonin syndrome due to citalopram (IMA final answer key, 2024-Sep, Q94).

Paroxetine’s **anticholinergic effects** may increase delirium risk. Beers 2023 lists it among strongly anticholinergic antidepressants to avoid in older adults (Hazzard p. 929; Beers p. 2059, Table 2).

**A. Delirium due to paroxetine.** Correct, officially accepted and source-supported: its anticholinergic effects can increase delirium risk, and Beers recommends avoiding it in older adults (Hazzard p. 929; Beers p. 2059).
**B. QT prolongation and torsades de pointes due to venlafaxine.** Wrong, not officially accepted. The venlafaxine row emphasizes dose-dependent hypertension, while the QT warning is in the citalopram row. This explains the table distinction without proving the proposed event impossible (p. 929).
**C. Orthostatic hypotension due to bupropion.** Wrong, not officially accepted. The table does list hypotension for bupropion but does not specify orthostatic hypotension; official scoring must be distinguished from the table’s inability to exclude all blood-pressure effects (p. 929).
**D. Serotonin syndrome due to citalopram.** Correct, accepted after appeal and correct for scoring. The existing caveat remains: the scenario does not describe a chain establishing serotonin syndrome, and the drug table lists other adverse effects. Official acceptance does not prove that this patient is expected to develop it (p. 929; note below).

The table states that paroxetine’s anticholinergic effects may increase delirium risk. Applying this warning to the proposed antidepressant in an older woman supports the paroxetine-delirium option. Citalopram-related serotonin syndrome was added in the post-appeal key, but no supporting chain was found in the scenario described (Hazzard pp. 883, 929; IMA September 2024, Q94).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 883, 929; AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Table 2, p. 2059. Official references and the existing caveat are retained in English.

q: מהם העקרונות בהמלצה לטיפול בנוגד דיכאון?
o: לתרופות נוגדות דיכאון יש מינון טיפולי אחיד
בדיכאון מינורי מומלץ מינון נמוך של תרופות נוגדות דיכאון
לתרופות נוגדות דיכאון יעילות גבוהה במטופלים עם דמנציה
לטיפול נוגד דיכאון יש אפקט פלסבו גבוה
explanation:
A **substantial placebo response** is a central feature of antidepressant treatment, particularly in less severe depression where the drug-placebo difference may be small. This limits the inference that every minor depression requires medication (p. 1014).

**A. Antidepressants have one uniform therapeutic dose.** Wrong, starting low and titrating permits individual adjustment; gradual titration may improve adherence, and the source does not prescribe one dose for everyone (p. 1015).
**B. Minor depression should be treated with low-dose antidepressants.** Wrong, a small drug-placebo difference in less severe depression does not create an automatic recommendation for low-dose medication in every minor depression (p. 1014).
**C. Antidepressants are highly effective in patients with dementia.** Wrong, the source summarizes numerous negative studies and questions their usefulness in dementia; high efficacy does not represent this evidence (p. 1015).
**D. Antidepressant treatment has a large placebo effect.** Correct, placebo responses can be substantial, and some studies show no statistically significant medication advantage, especially in less severe depression (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014-1015.
referenceNote: Paper cites pp.114–115, chapter 65; the verified depression treatment content is on pp.1014–1015.

q: מה מאפיין טיפול ב- Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) בגיל המבוגר?
o: טיפול ב-ECT פחות יעיל בזקנים לעומת צעירים
טיפול ב-ECT בטוח עם מעט תופעות לוואי
טיפול ב-ECT גורם לירידה בזיכרון לטווח ארוך
שיעור תסמיני הדיכאון גבוה אחרי טיפול ב-ECT
explanation:
**Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)** is at least as effective in older as younger adults, and older patients may respond better. The book describes high response and remission rates and a relatively safe current treatment with few adverse effects. It is an early option for severe or psychotic depression or limited medication response (p. 1014).

**A. ECT is less effective in older than younger patients.** Wrong, the source describes at least comparable and potentially greater responsiveness in older patients (p. 1014).
**B. ECT is safe with few adverse effects.** Correct, this is the official answer and the book's description of modern ECT; it is not a guarantee of no harm to an individual (p. 1014).
**C. ECT causes long-term memory decline.** Wrong, the source describes short-term memory loss that almost always resolves within weeks after treatment. Persistent decline is not the general feature sought here, but this does not exclude every memory-related adverse effect (p. 1014).
**D. Depressive symptoms remain high after ECT.** Wrong, the source emphasizes efficacy and high response/remission rates. Benefit can decay later, which is different from claiming a high level of depression as an immediate treatment outcome (p. 1014).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1014.

q: בת 90, גרה לבד בבית, תמיד היתה מאוד פעילה. לאחרונה מתלוננת על קושי לעשות עבודות בית קלות שבעבר הייתה עושה בקלות. בוצע מבחן PHQ-9 המצורף בתמונה מספר 4 לפי המבחן מה האבחנה ומה הטיפול?
o: מדובר ב- Dysthymia, מומלץ התחלת טיפול תרופתי
מדובר ב- Minor Depression מומלץ מעקב בלבד
יש לחפש גורם אחר לעייפות, מעקב בלבד
מדובר ב- Dysthymia, מומלץ טיפול פסיכותרפי
explanation:
Official answers: Minor depression, follow-up only; seek another cause of fatigue, follow-up only (IMA final answer key, June 2025, question 57).

The **PHQ-9 severity score and diagnostic symptom count are different measures**. In Figure 4, items 1, 2, 4 and 5 are marked several days producing a severity score of 4. The source counts these items diagnostically only at more than half the days or nearly every day; item 9, which has an exception, is marked zero. Thus the diagnostic count is zero and does not meet the minor-depression definition, although the official key accepts it; functional difficulty does not change symptom frequency (Hazzard p. 1011, Figure 65-2; IMA June 2025 album, PDF p. 3).

"Calculate the Total (Severity) Score: Multiply the assigned point values by the number of responses given by the patient in each frequency column." (Hazzard 8e, p. 1011.)
"with symptoms of 2 years, plus functional impairment (#10)" (Hazzard 8e, p. 1011, dysthymia row.)

**A. Dysthymia; start medication.** Wrong, the figure requires chronic symptoms for two years to consider dysthymia. The description and markings do not establish that duration, so they do not justify medication for this diagnosis (p. 1011).
**B. Minor depression; follow-up only.** Correct, officially accepted. However, the album markings do not meet the diagnostic symptom count for minor depression; the discrepancy must be understood rather than diagnosing it from the severity score alone (p. 1011; examination album, PDF p. 3).
**C. Look for another cause of fatigue; follow-up only.** Correct, officially accepted. Because the markings do not establish the proposed depressive diagnoses, seeking another explanation and following up is consistent with distinguishing a complaint from a questionnaire-based diagnosis (p. 1011; inference applied to album PDF p. 3).
**D. Dysthymia; psychotherapy.** Wrong, choosing psychotherapy does not supply the missing dysthymia criteria; the required duration is not documented (p. 1011).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1011, Figure 65-2; IMA June 2025 examination album, 1-based PDF p. 3.

q: מהם העקרונות בהמלצה לטיפול בנוגד דיכאון?
o: כדי להגיע לתגובה טיפולית חשוב להגיע למינון מטרה של התרופה
בטיפול בדיכאון מינורי מומלץ מינון נמוך של תרופות לעומת דיכאון מג'ורי מינון גבוה
תרופות נוגדות דיכאון יעילות מאוד במטופלים עם דמנציה
לטיפול נוגד דיכאון יש אפקט פלסבו גבוה
explanation:
A central point in antidepressant treatment is the **strong placebo effect**, especially in milder cases, where the medication-placebo difference is small. Monitoring and psychosocial intervention can sometimes be appropriate in mild cases (p. 1012).

**A. Reaching the drug's target dose is important for a therapeutic response.** Wrong, for official scoring. The book does not give a uniform dose that guarantees response; dosing should be individualized to benefit and tolerability (p. 1015).
**B. Minor depression requires a low dose, whereas major depression requires a high dose.** Wrong, the book does not support the idea that a little depression needs a little medication; benefit in minor depression has not been demonstrated to justify that dosing rule (p. 1015).
**C. Antidepressants are very effective in patients with dementia.** Wrong, many negative studies call their usefulness into question. Continuing treatment without measurable benefit adds medication burden (p. 1015).
**D. Antidepressant treatment has a strong placebo effect.** Correct, this is the official answer and is supported by the description of a powerful placebo response, especially in less severe depression (p. 1014).

The original option about reaching a target dose does not say that all drugs have the same dose; the source emphasizes individualized dosing and the absence of a standard dose guaranteeing response (p. 1015).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1012, 1014–1015.

q: On the PHQ-9 diagnostic algorithm, what specific additional criterion (beyond symptom count) distinguishes probable dysthymia from minor depression?
o: Question #2 (mood) with symptoms of 2 years
Functional impairment alone, regardless of duration
Question #1 alone instead of question #2
No requirement concerning depressed mood
explanation:
The PHQ-9 algorithm for probable dysthymia adds mood question 2 with symptoms for two years and functional impairment (p1011).

C. Question #1 alone instead of question #2: The probable dysthymia row specifically requires question 2 (p1011).
D. No requirement concerning depressed mood: Question 2, mood, is explicitly included (p1011).
B. Functional impairment alone, regardless of duration: Functional impairment is required in addition to the mood and two-year criterion, not instead of it (p1011).

q: Why might slow up-titration of an antidepressant improve adherence even though patients reach the same final dose either way?
o: A narrow therapeutic dosage window is the stated explanation for antidepressant adherence
More personalized attention and fewer side effects during titration
Slow titration usually produces a lower final dose in the comparison described
Higher starting doses produced better adherence
explanation:
**Slow titration can improve adherence even when the eventual dose is unchanged** (p. 1015). The chapter suggests that patients receive more personal attention during dose increases and experience fewer side effects; it presents these as likely explanations, rather than proving a single mechanism (p. 1015).
"More likely, the patient receives more personalized attention during dosage increases, and fewer side effects occur with titration." (p. 1015).

**A. A narrow therapeutic dosage window is the stated explanation for antidepressant adherence.** Wrong, the chapter does not support a fixed narrow therapeutic window across antidepressants as this adherence explanation; it emphasizes tolerability and individualized dosing (p. 1015).
**B. More personalized attention and fewer side effects during titration.** Correct, these are the chapter’s suggested reasons why gradual increases improved adherence despite the same eventual dose (p. 1015).
**C. Slow titration usually produces a lower final dose in the comparison described.** Wrong, the eventual doses were the same, so a lower final dose cannot explain the adherence difference in the comparison (p. 1015).
**D. Higher starting doses produced better adherence.** Wrong, better adherence occurred in those who started lower and titrated upward; starting higher did not produce the reported advantage (p. 1015).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e (marked), pp. 1015.
